title: Bandit-Gated Communication Budgets for Multi-Agent Workflows
research_question: Can a contextual bandit that adaptively decides when agents should communicate, query peers, or act independently reduce token cost and latency while preserving or improving task success in multi-agent AI workflows?
hypothesis: In multi-agent workflows, much communication is redundant; a contextual bandit that allocates communication only when estimated coordination value is high will outperform fixed communication patterns on cost-efficiency and maintain or improve end-task accuracy.
motivation: The knowledge base shows multiple rejected ideas around adaptive routing, dynamic replanning, and reflection-triggered communication, suggesting persistent interest in workflow adaptation but insufficient novelty in prior formulations. A clear gap is that these proposals focus on static policy design or heuristic triggers rather than online learning of communication value under budget constraints. Framing communication as a sequential decision problem with explicit token/latency budgets offers a more falsifiable and practically useful direction for agent orchestration.
